rows: Kitty Stieglitz

A girl holds a bowl of fruit in this color photograph. The Lumière brothers began selling Autochrome plates in 1907. They used tiny dyed grains of potato starch as color filters, and Stieglitz was one of the first artists to try them on his daughter Kitty.
How are the colors different from the colors in a modern photo?
Alfred Stieglitz
Gertrude Käsebier photographed her friend and fellow photographer Alfred Stieglitz in 1902, the year he founded the Photo-Secession, a group that fought to make photography respected as an art.
What does his face say about a man who was determined?
A Corner of Zuni
Edward S. Curtis photographed the adobe houses of Zuni Pueblo in New Mexico, stacked like steps with ladders to the upper levels. The pueblo has been lived in for hundreds of years.
How would you get up to the top floor?
The Flatiron
Stieglitz photographed the new Flatiron Building in a snowfall, its triangular shape rising behind a bare tree. He said it looked like the bow of a ship moving toward him.
Do you see why people compared the building to a ship?
Chief Joseph
Chief Joseph, a Nez Perce leader, led his people on a long, desperate journey in 1877 to avoid being forced onto a reservation. Edward Curtis photographed him in 1903, the year before he died.
What do you think he is thinking about?
The Wright Brothers' First Flight

On December 17, 1903, at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright flew the first powered airplane for twelve seconds and 120 feet. A man named John Daniels pressed the shutter of a camera aimed at the plane just as it left the ground, while Wilbur ran alongside.
Find the person running at the right. Who do you think it is?
A Madonna of the Tenements
Lewis Hine photographed an immigrant mother and her children at Ellis Island. Hine named it after paintings of Mary and the baby Jesus, to show that these families deserved respect.
What do you think this mother hopes for her children?
Moonlight: The Pond
Edward Steichen made this picture of a moonlit pond in New York by printing it in layers of green and blue pigment. It was one of the first photographs to sell for a high price.
Can you find the reflections of the trees?
Laborers at Work on the Panama Canal
In 1904 the United States began building a canal across Panama to link the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Thousands of workers, many from the Caribbean, dug through mountains in the hot sun.
What tools do you think they used?
Canyon de Chelly, Navajo
Edward S. Curtis photographed Navajo riders walking across the floor of a canyon in Arizona, tiny compared with the tall red cliffs. The picture is one of his most famous.
How tall do you think the cliffs are compared with the riders?
Richard Strauss
Richard Strauss was a German composer who wrote the music that opens the film 2001: A Space Odyssey. Edward Steichen photographed him in dramatic shadow.
What kind of music do you think he would write?
The Flatiron, Evening
Steichen photographed the Flatiron Building in rainy twilight, and printed it in blue-green tones with a few touches of color. The picture feels like a painting of a misty New York evening.
What time of day does it feel like?
A Boy's Grin
A boy in a cap breaks into a big grin. Lewis Hine photographed working children across the US, and often caught their personalities as well as their hard lives.
What do you think made him smile?
Fresh Air for the Baby
On a hot New York day, a baby sleeps on a cushion outside while an old man rests by the wall of a tenement. Crowded apartments were so stuffy that families took their children out into the street.
Where do you like to go when it's too hot at home?
Italian Immigrant at Ellis Island
Lewis Hine photographed new arrivals at Ellis Island, where about twelve million immigrants entered the United States. This young woman wears a headscarf and an open, serious expression.
What do you think she hoped to find in America?
Russian Family, Ellis Island
A family sits together on a bench in the great hall at Ellis Island, waiting to learn whether they can enter the country. Hine treated each family as individuals.
What would you pack if you were moving to another country?
Italian Family Seeking Lost Baggage
A family stands near piles of luggage at Ellis Island, looking for their lost bags. Hine's pictures show that arriving in a new country was hard.
What would be the first thing you'd look for?
Auguste Rodin
The French sculptor Auguste Rodin made The Thinker and many other famous statues. Gertrude Käsebier photographed him in Paris with his white beard glowing against a pale background.
What kind of things would a sculptor see in a block of stone?
